181000.reconstruction: A carrier representing the domain of binary relations over elements (7400), used to define structural properties like parent-child mappings and depth.

181001.reconstruction: A predicate on lists (7420) satisfied if the list contains no duplicate elements, effectively representing a set with extensional uniqueness.

181002.reconstruction: A predicate on two lists (7420) satisfied if every element of the first list is also an element of the second list (the subset relation).

181003.reconstruction: A predicate on two lists (7420) satisfied if they contain exactly the same elements regardless of order (extensional set equality).

181004.reconstruction: Defines a valid tree structure on nodes RL with parent relation P and root, where TG is an upward-closed subset of RL, and M maps entities EL to nodes. It includes a depth relation D to ensure well-foundedness.

181005.reconstruction: A predicate satisfied if node r is an element of set S and no child of r (according to relation P) is present in set S, identifying r as a leaf relative to the current set S.

181006.reconstruction: A predicate satisfied if node r is a leaf of set S (per 181005), is not a member of the target set TG, and is the image of entity e under mapping M.

181007.reconstruction: A predicate satisfied if set Sp is extensionally equal to set S excluding exactly one instance of node r.

181008.reconstruction: A predicate satisfied if set Sp is obtained by removing a valid removable node r (satisfying 181006 for entity e) from set S.

181009.reconstruction: A saturation predicate satisfied if no node in set S satisfies the removal conditions (181006) for entity e.

181010.reconstruction: A carrier for sequences (lists) of sets (7420), used to represent the execution trace of the node removal process.

181011.reconstruction: The constructor for an empty sequence of sets.

181012.reconstruction: The constructor for a non-empty sequence of sets, taking a head (set) and a tail (sequence of sets).

181013.reconstruction: The field accessor for the head set of a non-empty sequence of sets.

181014.reconstruction: The field accessor for the tail sequence of a non-empty sequence of sets.

181015.reconstruction: A predicate relating a sequence of sets (181010) to its natural number length (7000).

181016.reconstruction: A recursive predicate satisfied if tr is a trace of sets representing the step-by-step removal of all possible nodes for entity e, starting from set S and ending at a saturated set Sf.

181017.reconstruction: A recursive predicate satisfied if Sf is the result of sequentially applying the saturation process (181016) for each entity in the sequence T, starting from set S.

181018.reconstruction: A predicate satisfied if the sequence of entities T successfully reduces the initial set of nodes RL to exactly the target set TG within a valid tree structure.

181019.reconstruction: An optimization predicate satisfied if T is a sequence of entities that satisfies 181018 and no other valid sequence T2 has a strictly smaller length (per LEQ relation 7013).

global_reconstruction.input_structure: A tree-structured hierarchy of nodes (RL) with a designated root and a target subset (TG) that is upward-closed, plus a set of entities (EL) mapped to specific nodes.
global_reconstruction.well_formedness: The node sets must be unique lists; the parent relation must form a finite tree where every non-root node has exactly one parent; the target set must be a subset of the nodes and contain the parents of its members.
global_reconstruction.state_semantics: States are subsets of nodes; state equality is extensional (containing the same set of node identities).
global_reconstruction.local_action_semantics: An entity can remove a node from the current state if that node is a leaf in the current state, is not in the target set, and is mapped to by that entity.
global_reconstruction.saturation_semantics: For a single entity, the removal action is applied greedily and exhaustively until no further valid nodes for that entity remain in the state.
global_reconstruction.sequence_semantics: A sequence of entities is processed by executing the full saturation process for each entity in the order they appear in the sequence.
global_reconstruction.success_condition: The final state after processing the entire sequence of entities must be extensionally equal to the target set TG.
global_reconstruction.objective: Minimize the total number of entities in the sequence T required to reach the success condition.
